title: Progressive control-plane promotion with traffic-slicing and invariant gating
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: implement a progressive, traffic-sliced control-plane version promotion flow for Private (VPC) deployments using Terraform-managed IaC and a small orchestration shim. This ticket covers the Terraform module changes, health and invariant checks, automated promotion gates, and an operator-run canary verification loop.
motivation: Current private control-plane upgrades are either manual or coarse-grained (wave-based). We need a lower-risk path to roll forward control-plane versions in customer VPCs with measurable health gates, automated rollback on regressions, and a Terraform-first config model so SRE/Platform teams can adopt the same tooling used for provisioning.
success_criteria: Terraform module supports declarative 'promotion' resource with 'target_version', 'slice_percent', and 'check_profile' fields
Automated promotion runs can advance from 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% based on health gate pass/fail
Health checks include control-plane API latency p50/p95, leader stability, reconciliation errors, and KV-store operation latency
Rollback occurs automatically on gate failure and appears in control plane audit logs
Operators can trigger manual hold/advance via Console and Terraform plan shows only promotion-safe diffs
Integration test harness simulates VPC with 3 clusters and verifies promotion gating logic in CI
non_goals: Not implementing cross-region traffic mirroring (out of scope for initial rollout)
Not reworking tenant-level scheduling; this ticket focuses on control plane components only
No user-facing API changes in the hosted Redwood API
implementation_plan: Design Terraform module: sources/infra/modules/controlplane/promotion.tf with resources: redwoodctl_promotion, redwoodctl_health_profile
Implement promotion controller (small Go binary): reads promotion CR equivalent state via Terraform output and advances according to timers and health signals
Add health probes exported to Console: ctlplane_api_latency, operator_reconcile_errors, raft_election_rate
Wire in audit logging to customer control plane audit log bucket and internal ops-destination
Add feature flag (private.upgrade.progressive) for initial rollouts
Create CI integration tests using local KinD + mock KV backend to validate gating logic
Document runbook and rollback steps in Confluence and include PR link in ticket
acceptance_criteria: Terraform plan for promotion shows only resource-change 'promotion' with no destructive diffs to core control plane resources
Promotion controller respects configured 'slice_percent' schedule and aborts when any gate metric crosses threshold
Unit and integration tests added to repo pass in main branch
Feature flag gating allows opt-in for early customers
Eng-oncall sign-off after 2 staged promotions in staging environment
tasks: T1: Draft Terraform module schema and variables (Arjun)
T3: Define health checks and SLA thresholds with SRE (Kendall)
T4: Console UI prototype for manual hold/advance (Design + Frontend)
T5: CI integration harness to simulate promotions
T6: Documentation: runbook + PRD + customer-facing notes
risks: Incorrect health profiles could cause repeated rollbacks or delayed rollouts
Terraform plan drift if promotion controller mutates resources outside of Terraform expectations
Customer-side network policy differences may make slice traffic distribution non-uniform
Audit/logging gaps could make troubleshooting post-failure difficult
mitigations: Keep promotion controller write-path limited to a single 'promotion' resource and expose status only; Terraform remains the source of truth
Add conservative default thresholds and require opt-in feature flag for customers on first wave
Run synthetic traffic generator during promotion slices in staging to validate distribution
Include an explicit post-failure diagnostic artifact (bundle) that collects logs and metrics for the oncall to triage
runbook_summary: If a promotion gate fails: 1) controller auto-rolls back slice to previous version; 2) mark promotion as 'failed' in audit log; 3) oncall runs diagnostic bundle and opens ENG incident if customer impact > medium; 4) optionally escalate to release team for hotfix or revert in Terraform.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on Terraform module surface area and the 'no destructive diffs' guarantee. Also check the promotion controller's pact with Terraform (status-only writes). Security review for audit log destinations is queued separately.
